les: Geboue met 'n werk om te doen
kaps_punt: Geboue in verskillende plekke en hul gebruike - geboue soos huise, diereskuilings, winkels, skole, klinieke, banke, kantore, plekke van aanbidding, fabrieke, motorhuise en treinstasies

items.bewering: Mense het elkeen van hierdie geboue ontwerp en gebou om 'n bepaalde werk te doen. Daardie werk gee vir mense iets wat hulle nodig het of gebruik.
items.blok: Mense bou vir 'n rede
items.bron: Designing Buildings Wiki and Wikipedia, 'Form follows function' (https://designingbuildings.co.uk/wiki/Form_follows_function ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Form_follows_function): a building's purpose drives its design. The universal 'elkeen' holds because it is about why a building was first built; a building later put to another use (a house turned into an office) was still built for a purpose, and the sentence does not say the purpose never changes. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Sommige van hierdie geboue voorsien in 'n behoefte van die mense daar. 'n Behoefte is iets wat mense nodig het om veilig en gesond te leef.
items.blok: Mense bou vir 'n rede
items.bron: Law Insider and USLegal, 'basic needs' (https://lawinsider.com/dictionary/basic-needs ; https://definitions.uslegal.com/b/basic-needs/): the minimum requirements for survival and well-being, including food, water, shelter, clothing and healthcare. 'Veilig en gesond leef' is a fair Grade 4 simplification of survival and well-being. 'Sommige' is correctly narrow: a shop selling food or a clinic serves a need, but not every building on the list does. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Iets wat mense nodig het om veilig en gesond te leef.
items.blok: behoefte
items.bron: As above (Law Insider, USLegal, 'basic needs'). The glossary entry matches the study-text definition word for word and is true when read on its own. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Huise en woonstelle voorsien in die behoefte aan skuiling.
items.blok: Huise gee skuiling
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'shelter' (https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/shelter_1): 'the fact of having a place to live or stay, considered as a basic human need'. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Skuiling is 'n plek wat mense of diere veilig hou en teen wind, reën, koue en hitte beskerm.
items.blok: Huise gee skuiling
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'shelter' (protection from rain, danger or attack; the wind example); Vocabulary.com, 'shelter' (https://vocabulary.com/dictionary/shelter): a structure that protects you from the elements. Cold and heat fall under 'the elements'; protection from heat and sun appears in the Cal Poly housing note (https://grandavehousing.calpoly.edu/news/shelters-meaning-a-deep-dive). The definition covers animals as well as people, which matches the farm sentence after it. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: 'n Plek wat mense of diere veilig hou en teen wind, reën, koue en hitte beskerm.
items.blok: skuiling
items.bron: As above (Oxford Learner's, Vocabulary.com, 'shelter'). Identical to the study-text definition and true on its own. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Op 'n plaas bou mense ook 'n stal of 'n hok wat die diere teen reën en koue beskerm.
items.blok: Huise gee skuiling
items.bron: RSPCA Assured, cold-weather advice to farmers (https://www.rspcaassured.org.uk/press/temperatures-drop): dry shelters that keep animals safe from wind, rain and snow; Beef + Lamb NZ shelter fact sheet (https://beeflambnz.com/sites/default/files/factsheets/pdfs/fact-sheet-174-shelter_0.pdf). The relative clause ('wat die diere ... beskerm') limits the claim to roofed stables and coops, so it does not claim that an open kraal keeps out rain. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Winkel: mense koop hier kos, klere en ander goed wat hulle nodig het.
items.blok: Elke gebou het sy eie werk
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'shop': a building or part of a building where you can buy goods or services. True as stated; it does not say every shop sells all three. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Skool: kinders leer hier lees en skryf en baie ander dinge.
items.blok: Elke gebou het sy eie werk
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'school': a place where children go to be educated. Reading and writing are the foundation of the South African school curriculum (literacy in the Foundation Phase). Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Kliniek: 'n verpleegster of 'n dokter help siek mense en gee inentings.
items.blok: Elke gebou het sy eie werk
items.bron: GCIS South Africa Yearbook 2009, Health chapter (https://www.gcis.gov.za/sites/default/files/docs/resourcecentre/yearbook/2009/chapter12.pdf): a network of government clinics is the backbone of primary and preventive health care, and primary health care workers provide immunisation among other services. PMC3306367 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3306367) and the KwaZulu-Natal study on doctors visiting clinics (https://www.nisc.co.za/products/abstracts/19552/): clinics are usually staffed by nurses, and doctors visit. Putting the nurse first with 'of' matches South African practice. PMC4887596 confirms that professional nurses in rural clinics deliver the immunisation programme. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Bank: mense hou hulle geld hier veilig en kan dit weer gaan haal.
items.blok: Elke gebou het sy eie werk
items.bron: FDIC Money Smart for Kids (https://www.fdic.gov/consumer-resource-center/money-smart-basics-kids-full-packet.pdf) and KidsMoney (https://www.kidsmoney.org/?p=2221): a bank looks after deposited money and the account holder can withdraw it. Simplification noted: the bank keeps a record of the deposit and lends the money on, rather than storing each person's notes. The sentence does not say the notes are stored, so a learner reasoning further is not led anywhere false at Grade 4. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Kantoor: mense werk hier by lessenaars met papiere en rekenaars.
items.blok: Elke gebou het sy eie werk
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'office' (https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/office): a room, set of rooms or building where people work, usually sitting at desks; Merriam-Webster, the same sense. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Plek van aanbidding: mense kom hier bymekaar om saam te aanbid.
items.blok: Elke gebou het sy eie werk
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Place of worship' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_of_worship): a structure or space where individuals or a congregation come for acts of devotion; Vocabulary.com, 'place of worship': any building where congregations gather for prayer. The wording is neutral across religions. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Fabriek: 'n gebou waar mense of masjiene baie van dieselfde produk maak om te verkoop.
items.blok: Elke gebou het sy eie werk
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'factory' (https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/factory): a building or group of buildings where goods are made, mainly by machine; Auslan dictionary, 'factory': machines used to make goods in large quantities. 'Baie van dieselfde produk' captures large-quantity production. It does not say a factory makes only one product. 'Om te verkoop' holds for commercial manufacture. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: 'n Gebou waar mense of masjiene baie van dieselfde produk maak om te verkoop.
items.blok: fabriek
items.bron: As above (Oxford Learner's, Auslan, 'factory'). Identical to the list item and true on its own. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Motorhuis: hier hou mense hulle motor uit die reën en die son.
items.blok: Elke gebou het sy eie werk
items.bron: Global Symbols / Blissymbolics, 'garage' (https://globalsymbols.com/symbolsets/blissymbolics/symbols/9129): Afrikaans 'garage, motorhuis'; Dictionary.com, 'garage' (https://dictionary.com/browse/Garage): a building or indoor area for parking or storing motor vehicles. I could not reach an online Afrikaans dictionary entry for 'motorhuis' (the VivA search page returned 404). The equivalence rests on the bilingual listing and the meaning of the English word. True as stated. For whoever owns coverage, not a fact error: the English CAPS word is 'garages', which in South African English often means a filling station or workshop. The lesson follows the Afrikaans CAPS word 'motorhuise', the domestic sense. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Treinstasie: treine stop hier sodat mense kan opklim en afklim.
items.blok: Elke gebou het sy eie werk
items.bron: EEA GEMET thesaurus, 'railway station' (https://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/en/concept/11269): a place along a route or line at which a train stops to pick up or let off passengers or goods. The lesson leaves out goods. That is an omission, not a falsehood. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Nie elke plek het al hierdie geboue nie. Op 'n plaas is daar gewoonlik nie 'n treinstasie nie.
items.blok: Nie elke plek het alles nie
items.bron: GEMET, 'railway station': a station is a stopping point on a railway line, usually with buildings and services, and it serves a town or settlement rather than one farm. 'Gewoonlik' allows for the rare rural siding or halt; Wikipedia, 'Railway station types in Germany' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Railway_station_types_in_Germany) notes minor 'halts' and 'flag stops'. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Die lys hierbo wys waarvoor mense bou en nie wat in elke plek staan nie.
items.blok: Nie elke plek het alles nie
items.bron: This is a statement about the lesson itself, and it matches the list block's content: the list gives a use for each building and makes no claim about where any of them stand. Nothing outside the lesson to check. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Twee skole in twee dorpe doen dieselfde werk en lyk tog nie altyd eenders nie. Die werk binne die gebou help bepaal sy grootte en sy vorm.
items.blok: Hoekom lyk twee skole nie altyd eenders nie?
items.bron: Wikipedia and Designing Buildings Wiki, 'Form follows function': Sullivan held that a building's size and massing should follow from its function. Both sources also note that one function can be met in several forms, which fits 'help bepaal' and 'nie altyd eenders nie'. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Die klimaat van die plek speel ook 'n rol. Geboue in 'n streek met baie reën kry dikwels steiler dakke.
items.blok: Hoekom lyk twee skole nie altyd eenders nie?
items.bron: Vault, history of roofing (https://legacy.vault.com/industries-professions/professions/r/roofers/history): flat roofs have historically gone with dry climates, and pitched roofs with climates where drainage matters; Encyclopaedia Britannica 7th ed. 1842, roof entry (https://jimclifford.ca/early_encyclopedia_britannica/articles/1842/eb_7th_1842_015774.html): a high-pitched roof sheds rain and snow better than a low one; BRANZ, resilient roof design (https://www.branz.co.nz/design-build/articles/resilient-roof-design-and-construction). The sources also say pitch depends on the roofing material and on style. 'Dikwels' is the right strength, and the sentence does not say climate alone decides. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Mense bou ook met materiaal soos klip of klei wat naby hulle lê.
items.blok: Hoekom lyk twee skole nie altyd eenders nie?
items.bron: Franco Frescura, indigenous architecture of southern Africa, SA History Online (https://sahistory.org.za/francofrescura/indiginous-architecture-index.html): rural dwellings were traditionally built from saplings, timber, clay, grass and dung, with stone rubble and shale used in some regions. The architecture draws on its physical environment. The sentence states a tendency with 'ook' and does not say all building uses local material, so it holds for modern brick-and-concrete schools as well. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Die gebou se grootte hang ook af van hoeveel mense dit gebruik. 'n Skool vir duisend kinders het meer klaskamers as 'n klein plaasskool.
items.blok: Hoekom lyk twee skole nie altyd eenders nie?
items.bron: Sowetan, 'The school with 13 pupils and a teacher' (https://www.sowetanlive.co.za/news/2014-09-13-the-school-with-13-pupils-and-a-teacher/); Mail & Guardian, 'Glimpse into a different world' (https://mg.co.za/news/education/2009-05-04-glimpse-into-a-different-world/): small South African farm schools are allocated one to three educators and often combine grades in one classroom. 'Duisend kinders' is an illustrative size, not a figure presented as measured. The comparison is direct, not an analogy, and its mapping holds. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Hierdie dinge werk saam wanneer mense 'n gebou beplan. Twee geboue met dieselfde werk kan dus in twee plekke anders lyk.
items.blok: Hoekom lyk twee skole nie altyd eenders nie?
items.bron: The conclusion follows from the three factors already verified above (function: 'Form follows function'; climate: Vault and Britannica 1842; local material: Frescura, SAHO). 'Kan' is correctly modal. Full check, this round.

opsomming: Elke kontroleerbare bewering in al agt blokke is teen bronne nagegaan en waar bevind (die les bevat geen oortreffende trap en geen analogie nie, en die begrip-inskrywings is alleen gelees ook waar), en vir die mens wat dekking hanteer: die Engelse KABV se 'garages' kan in Suid-Afrikaanse Engels 'n vulstasie beteken, terwyl die les die Afrikaanse KABV se 'motorhuise' in die huishoudelike betekenis volg, wat waar is maar nie 'n feitefout is nie.
